# NAND parts this OpenWrt build can drive - Xiaomi AX3000T / RD03v2 (IPQ5018)
#
# Generated by tools/mknand-support.sh from the kernel that was actually
# built (Linux 6.12.94, drivers/mtd/nand/spi, vendor tables: alliancememory, ato, esmt, etron, fmsh, foresee, gigadevice, macronix, micron, paragon, skyhigh, toshiba, winbond, xtx).
#
# Format, one part per line, '#' starts a comment:
#
#     <flash_type>  <mfr:dev>  <part>
#
# flash_type is the device byte the stock bootloader leaves in the U-Boot
# environment after it probes the chip. That is how a unit self-identifies
# BEFORE anything is flashed:
#
#     fw_printenv flash_type      # OpenWrt
#     nvram get flash_type        # stock firmware
#
# An installer should read that byte and require a matching line here:
#
#     ft=$(fw_printenv -n flash_type)
#     grep -qi "^${ft}[[:space:]]" nand-support.txt || abort
#
# A flash_type of '-' means the kernel knows the part but the stock
# bootloader has no ID for it. Such a chip cannot be this board's boot NAND
# (the bootloader could not read it to boot in the first place), so those
# lines are informational: the driver would handle the part, this board
# will never present it.
#
# 12 of the 12 parts in the bootloader's own table are supported, and this
# driver knows 112 parts in total.
#
# --- parts the stock bootloader can also identify ---------------------------
# column 3 is the bootloader's name for the part; the comment is what the
# kernel's own table calls it, which is what actually proves support.
